prompt:
A student measures the thickness of a single sheet of paper (approximately 0.10 mm). Three instruments are available:
Instrument 1: Metre rule (resolution 1 mm)
Instrument 2: Vernier calipers (resolution 0.1 mm)
Instrument 3: Micrometer screw gauge (resolution 0.01 mm)
Which instrument should be selected, and why?
options: Instrument 1, because a 1 mm resolution covers the entire length of the paper.
Instrument 2, because its resolution is equal to the quantity being measured.
Instrument 3, because its resolution is much smaller than the thickness being measured, allowing reliable quantification.
Any of the three instruments, because instrument resolution has no bearing on measurement reliability.

answer.explanation: To make a meaningful measurement, the instrument resolution must be substantially smaller than the quantity being measured. A micrometer (0.01 mm resolution) is 10 times finer than the 0.10 mm paper thickness.

distractor_explanations: A 1 mm resolution cannot measure a 0.10 mm dimension; the paper is far smaller than a single division.
When resolution equals the dimension (0.1 mm), the reading is at best 0.1 mm with 100% reading uncertainty, unable to detect small variations.
Correct. The micrometer resolution (0.01 mm) is an order of magnitude smaller than 0.10 mm, providing sufficient detail.
Resolution directly determines whether a measurement is physically feasible.
hints: Compare the size of the object (0.10 mm) with the smallest division of each instrument.
A reliable measurement requires the instrument resolution to be much smaller than the measured quantity.
solution: Instrument 3 (micrometer screw gauge), because its 0.01 mm resolution is much finer than the 0.10 mm thickness.
teacher_walkthrough: Metre rule: resolution 1 mm > 0.10 mm. Completely unusable.
Vernier callipers: resolution 0.1 mm = dimension. Can only register 0 or 0.1 mm (huge fractional uncertainty).
Micrometer: resolution 0.01 mm gives ~10 discrete steps across the thickness, providing genuine measurement.

provenance.independence_statement: Authored apparatus selection problem based on ratio of quantity size to scale resolution.
